info.title: Business Application Platform API (BAPI)
info.description:
The Business Application Platform API is the legacy control plane behind the Power Platform admin centre. It manages environments and their lifecycle, Managed Environments, environment groups, DLP policies, tenant settings, tenant isolation, enterprise policies and admin application registration.

Most mutations are **asynchronous**: a `202` returns an absolute poll URL in `Location` (or `Operation-Location`) that renders a `LifecycleOperation`, whose `state.id` runs `NotStarted` → `Running` → `Succeeded`/`Failed`.

`api-version` is per operation rather than global, and the `PowerPlatform.Governance` paths take none at all. Sovereign clouds serve the same paths from their own hosts.

Unofficial and reverse-engineered — see the [README](https://github.com/AdamCoulterOz/powerplatform-apis/tree/main/bapi) for how it was derived and which parts are verified.

post.description:
Provisions an environment. `properties.displayName` and `properties.environmentSku` are mandatory; everything else is optional, and the service validates them in that order.

Dataverse is opt-in through `properties.databaseType`: setting it to `CommonDataService` provisions an organization from `properties.linkedEnvironmentMetadata`.

An environment without Dataverse is created synchronously in seconds; one with Dataverse is asynchronous. Either way the environment is readable before its `linkedEnvironmentMetadata` is, so clients that need the organization URL must keep re-reading after the operation succeeds.

A typical create body carries `location`, `displayName`, `environmentSku`, `databaseType`, `linkedEnvironmentMetadata` (`baseLanguage`, `currency.code`, an empty `templates`), `billingPolicy` and `cluster.category`. An explicit `null` is accepted wherever the member is optional, which is how `usedBy`, `parentEnvironmentGroup` and `governanceConfiguration` are normally sent.

x-notes.note: Sending `linkedEnvironmentMetadata` without `properties.databaseType` does not create a Dataverse organization and does not fail. The whole block is discarded and the call returns a successful, Dataverse-less environment with no error and no warning.

parameters.name: retainOnProvisionFailure
parameters.description: When true, a failed provision leaves the environment behind in a failed state for diagnosis instead of rolling it back. The admin center sends `false` explicitly.

parameters.name: overrideEnvironmentGroupAssigned
parameters.description: Lets `properties.parentEnvironmentGroup` win over whatever group the tenant's environment-group routing rules would otherwise assign — including `null`, which is how the admin center creates an ungrouped environment in a tenant that has a default group. The admin center sends `true` on every create.

201.description: Created synchronously, which is what an environment without Dataverse does. The body is the full created environment — its `name` is the new environment id, and `properties.provisioningState` is already `Succeeded`.

202.description: Accepted; provisioning continues asynchronously, which is what requesting Dataverse does. Poll the URL in `Location` (or `Operation-Location`); the finished operation's `links.environment.path` ends in the new environment id, and is the only place this response hands it back.

Location.description: Absolute poll URL, already carrying the request's api-version and any `$expand`. Present on every asynchronous response except `modifySku`, which uses `Operation-Location` instead; read whichever is set.

Operation-Location.description: The same poll URL under the alternate header name.

Retry-After.description: Suggested poll interval in seconds — always delta-seconds, never an HTTP date. Typically 3 to 5 seconds for creates, 5 for edits and Managed Environments changes, and 30 for deletes; the poll responses themselves suggest 10.

400.description: Rejected before provisioning. `EnvironmentDisplayNameNotFound` for a missing `properties.displayName`, `InvalidEnvironmentSku` (naming the SKU `NotSpecified`) for a missing `properties.environmentSku`, `EnvironmentLocationUnsupported` for an unknown `location`.

Links (`action=link`) or unlinks (`action=unlink`) an Azure enterprise policy — network injection, customer-managed key or managed identity — to the environment. `environmentType` names the policy kind and the body carries the Azure policy's `systemId`.

post.description:
Sets the environment's governance configuration. `protectionLevel: "Standard"` with a `settings.extendedSettings` block enables Managed Environments; `protectionLevel: "Basic"` disables it and ignores any settings sent alongside.

Managed Environments requires a linked Dataverse organization: on an environment without one the request is rejected outright rather than queued.

Every value inside `extendedSettings` is a string, including the booleans and the numbers.

The body is optional, and a bodyless POST — `Content-Length: 0`, no body at all — means enable with defaults: the service answers 202 with an `EnableGovernanceConfiguration` lifecycle operation and `Retry-After: 5`. Send a body only to set `settings.extendedSettings` at the same time.

get.description:
Polls an asynchronous operation. This is a first-class path, addressable directly at `api-version=2021-04-01`, and not merely the target of a `Location` header. Following the absolute URL an asynchronous response hands back is still the safer default: it carries the originating request's api-version and `$expand`.

`state.id` moves `NotStarted` → `Running` → `Succeeded`/`Failed`; a short operation can be `Succeeded` on the first poll. `stages` breaks the work into `Validate`, `Prepare`, `Run` and `Finalize`, which is where a failure localises. For a create, `links.environment.path` ends in the new environment's id — the only place an asynchronous create hands it back.

The operation record outlives its subject: a delete operation stays readable after the environment itself is gone.

patch.description:
Patches environment properties. Three request shapes are in use: a general `Environment` patch (display name, description, cadence, linked-metadata fields), a `GenerativeAiFeatures` patch, and a `DisasterRecoveryPatch`. Only the members sent are applied.

Pin api-version 2021-04-01. Newer versions turn Managed Environments on as a side effect of a description-only update.

The poll URL returned in `Location` preserves the request's `$expand` and api-version query string verbatim, so it can be fetched as-is. A succeeded lifecycle operation does not guarantee the next read reflects the change: the regional write and the read replica converge separately.

azureRegion.description: Concrete Azure region inside the location; assignable at create only where the location lists it.

databaseType.description: `CommonDataService` when a Dataverse organization is linked, `None` when not. On create this field is the switch that turns Dataverse on.

environmentSku.description: The environment type. `Default` is the tenant's built-in environment, `Developer` a personal one from the Developer Plan, `Trial` a time-limited one, and `Sandbox`/`Production` the pair `modifySku` converts between.

provisioningState.description: `Succeeded` when the environment is usable, `LinkedDatabaseProvisioning` while Dataverse is being provisioned into it, and `Deleting` between a delete request and the environment disappearing.

bingChatEnabled.description: Copilot answer grounding via Bing web search.

m365Enabled.description: Copilot grounding on Microsoft 365 service data.

addons.description: Purchased add-on capacity attached to the environment (AI Builder credits and similar). Empty unless the tenant has bought add-ons and assigned them here.

apiManagementAccountResourceId.description: Azure resource id of the API Management account backing the environment's connectors. Returned only on the `scopes/service` projection that `provisionInstance` answers with.

appDraftingCopilotEnabled.description: Whether makers may use the Copilot that drafts apps from a prompt.

capacity.description: Per-capacity-type consumption. A `$expand=properties.capacity` projection: absent from the list endpoint, and an empty array until the environment has consumed anything.

connectedGroups.description: Microsoft 365 groups (Teams-created environments) bound to this environment. Empty outside Teams environments.

creationType.description: `User` for an environment somebody created; `DefaultTenant` for the tenant's automatically provisioned default environment.

enableAnalyticsForMakers.description: Whether makers (not just admins) can see app and flow analytics here.

isDefault.description: True for the single tenant default environment, which cannot be deleted.

lifecycleAuthority.description: Which service owns this environment's lifecycle; set when the environment is driven by something other than the admin center.

retentionPeriod.description: ISO 8601 duration a deleted environment stays recoverable. `P7D`; duplicated inside `retentionDetails`.

trialScenarioType.description: Which trial programme an environment was created under; `None` for environments that are not trials.

environmentType.description: Coarse classification used by the maker portal, distinct from `environmentSku`: a `Sandbox` SKU environment still reports `Production` here. Absent from admin-scope reads.

azureRegionHint.description: The Azure region the environment was *requested* in, kept alongside the region it actually landed in. Returned by the maker scope where the admin scope returns `azureRegion`; the two normally agree.

scheduledLifecycleOperations.description: Lifecycle operations the platform has already scheduled against this environment — how a trial or an inactive Developer environment announces its own disablement and deletion dates before they happen. Returned only under `$expand=properties/scheduledLifecycleOperations`.

permissions.description: What the calling user may do in this environment, keyed by permission name. Returned only under `$expand=properties.permissions` on the maker scope; the key set is the grant, so a permission the caller lacks is absent rather than present-and-false.

EnvironmentProperties.description: Everything about an environment other than its identity. Several members are projections that only materialise when named in `$expand`.

disablePreferredDataLocationForTeamsEnvi.description: Stops Teams-created environments honouring the user's Microsoft 365 preferred data location, placing them in the tenant's default geography instead.

flexRoutingEnabled.description: Lets the platform place a routed environment in whichever geo has capacity rather than pinning it to the tenant's default one. Not returned on every tenant.

EnvironmentTemplate.description: Environment templates grouped by the SKU allowed to use them; a template can appear in several buckets. Every bucket is present even when empty: `standard` and `premium` are typically empty while the SKU-named buckets carry the content.

EnvironmentUserRequest.description: Grants and revocations applied in one call. Both lists may be sent together; the service applies removals and additions independently and reports each.

EnvironmentUserResponse.description: Per-item outcome for each requested grant and revocation. An overall 200 does not mean every item succeeded — check `httpStatus` on each.

ExtendedSettings.description: The Managed Environments settings. **Every value here is a string, including the booleans and the numbers** — `"true"`, `"false"`, `"-1"`. That is how the service returns them, and how it expects them on the way in.

excludeEnvironmentFromAnalysis.description: `"true"` suppresses the [weekly usage-insights digest](https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/managed-environment-usage-insights) for this environment and leaves it out of tenant-level analysis.

includeOnHomepageInsights.description: `"true"` surfaces this environment's insights on the admin center home page.

isGroupSharingDisabled.description: `"true"` stops makers sharing canvas apps with security groups, leaving only individual sharing. See [Managed Environment sharing limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/managed-environment-sharing-limits?tabs=new#canvas-app-sharing-rules).

limitSharingMode.description: `excludeSharingToSecurityGroups` bars security groups from canvas-app sharing; `noLimit` allows them. Paired with `maxLimitUserSharing`.

maxLimitUserSharing.description: Cap on how many individual users a canvas app may be shared with, as a decimal string. `"-1"` means no cap, and is the only valid value when `isGroupSharingDisabled` is `"false"`.

solutionCheckerMode.description: [Solution checker enforcement](https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/managed-environment-solution-checker) on solution import: `none` skips the scan, `warn` imports but reports findings, `block` refuses imports that fail.

solutionCheckerRuleOverrides.description: Comma-separated solution-checker rule ids to exempt (for example `meta-remove-dup-reg,web-use-async`); empty string exempts nothing.

suppressValidationEmails.description: `"true"` emails makers only when solution checker blocks an import; `"false"` also emails on warnings.

disableAiGeneratedDescriptions.description: `"true"` stops the platform generating app and flow descriptions with AI.

solutionCloudFlows-limitSharingMode.description: `disableSharing` blocks sharing of solution-aware cloud flows entirely; `noLimit` allows it. See [Solution-aware cloud flow sharing rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/managed-environment-sharing-limits?tabs=new#solution-aware-cloud-flow-sharing-rules).

solutionCloudFlows-maxLimitUserSharing.description: Cap on individual users a solution-aware cloud flow may be shared with. `"-1"` means no cap.

bot-authoringSharingDisabled.description: `"true"` stops Power Automate Copilot granting `Editor` permissions when an agent is shared. See [Agent sharing rules](https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/managed-environment-sharing-limits?tabs=new#agent-sharing-rules).

bot-limitSharingMode.description: `disableSharing` blocks granting `Viewer` permissions when a Copilot agent is shared; `noLimit` allows it.

bot-maxLimitUserSharing.description: Cap on individual users a Copilot agent may be shared with. `"-1"` means no cap.

powerPolicyLastModified.description: When these settings last changed. Service-populated; sending it has no effect.

GenerativeAiFeatures.description: PATCH body for the Copilot and generative-AI toggles.

bingChatEnabled.description: See EnvironmentProperties.bingChatEnabled; pointer semantics — omitted fields are left untouched.

GenerativeAiFeaturesProperties.description: Only the members present are applied; omitted ones keep their current values. Send just the members being changed.

protectionLevel.description: `Standard` turns Managed Environments on and makes `settings` meaningful; `Basic` turns it off.

GovernanceConfiguration.description: Whether the environment is a [Managed Environment](https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/managed-environment-overview), and the premium governance settings that come with it.

disableAdminDigest.description: Turns off the periodic admin digest email.

disableDeveloperEnvironmentCreationByNon.description: Stops non-admins creating Developer Plan environments for themselves.

enableDefaultEnvironmentRouting.description: Routes new makers into a personal developer environment instead of the shared default one.

environmentRoutingAllMakers.description: Routes every maker; when false only those in `environmentRoutingTargetSecurityGroupId` are routed.

environmentRoutingTargetEnvironmentGroup.description: Environment group the routed environments are created inside, so group governance applies to them.

environmentRoutingTargetSecurityGroupId.description: Entra group whose members are routed, when `environmentRoutingAllMakers` is false.

GovernanceSettings.description: Tenant-wide governance: who may create environments and where new makers land.

disableCopilot.description: Master switch turning Copilot off across the tenant.

enableOpenAiBotPublishing.description: Allows publishing agents backed by Azure OpenAI models.

disableAiPrompts.description: Blocks makers building custom AI prompts.

disableCopilotFeedback.description: Stops users sending feedback on Copilot responses.

disableCopilotFeedbackMetadata.description: Keeps feedback but strips the prompt and response metadata from it.

name.description: The template id sent as an entry of `linkedEnvironmentMetadata.templates`.

ItemDisabledReason.description: Why a template is unavailable to this tenant.

code.description: `DynamicsEntitlementMissing` — the tenant holds no licence for the application — is the reason a template comes back disabled.

httpStatus.description: Per-item status code, as a string. This is where a partial failure surfaces.

ItemResponse.description: The outcome of one grant or revocation.

name.description: The LCID as a string; the same value as `properties.localeId`.

Language.description: A base language offered for new Dataverse organizations in one location.

localeId.description: The LCID (for example 1033 for en-US) used as `baseLanguage` at environment creation.

localizedName.description: The language's name in its own language; `displayName` is the same name in the caller's.

isTenantDefault.description: True for the tenant's own language; exactly one entry carries it.

disableBillingPolicyCreationByNonAdminUs.description: Reserves pay-as-you-go billing policy creation to tenant admins.

enableTenantCapacityReportForEnvironment.description: Exposes the tenant-wide capacity report to environment admins.

storageCapacityConsumptionWarningThresho.description: Percentage of tenant storage capacity at which admins are warned.

enableTenantLicensingReportForEnvironmen.description: Exposes the tenant-wide licensing report to environment admins.

disableUseOfUnassignedAIBuilderCredits.description: Stops environments drawing on the tenant's unassigned AI Builder credit pool.

enableTenantSummaryReportForEnvironmentA.description: Exposes the tenant summary report to environment admins.

applyAutoClaimToOnlyManagedEnvironments.description: Restricts automatic premium-licence claim to Managed Environments, so unmanaged environments never consume tenant licences on a user's first premium action. Not returned on every tenant.

LicenseSettings.description: What environment admins may see and do with tenant licensing and capacity.

path.description: Note the shape: `links.environment.path` points at `/providers/Microsoft.BusinessAppPlatform/environments/{id}` — the unscoped path, not the `scopes/admin` one reads use. Its last segment is the environment id, which is how a create recovers the id it just made.

LifecycleLink.description: A path under the BAPI host, without scheme or host.

LifecycleOperation.description: One asynchronous BAPI operation. Reached by following the URL a 202 hands back in `Location` or `Operation-Location`, which is absolute and already carries the api-version (and any `$expand`) of the request that started it. Poll until `state.id` is `Succeeded` or `Failed`.

typeDisplayName.description: Localised label for `type.id`, as the admin center shows it. Mostly the id verbatim (`Create`, `Edit`), but not always: `EnableGovernanceConfiguration` renders as `Enable Managed Environment` and `UpdateGovernanceConfiguration` as `Update Managed Environment`.

stages.description: The operation's internal phases, in order. Useful for progress reporting; the failing stage names what went wrong.

LifecycleStage.description: One phase of a lifecycle operation. The four run in order: `Validate`, `Prepare`, `Run`, `Finalize`.

systemId.description: The Azure resource id of the enterprise policy.

LinkEnterprisePolicy.description: The link/unlink request: the Azure policy to act on.

LinkedAppMetadata.description: The Dynamics 365 first-party application deployed into the environment, when it was created from an application template.

backgroundOperationsState.description: Whether background flows/jobs are running or administratively paused.

domainName.description: The chosen Dataverse subdomain, tenant-unique across Power Platform. Must start with a letter and contain only `A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9` and `-`; `validateEnvironmentDetails` checks both the pattern and availability. A released domain name stays reserved for up to 24 hours.

instanceUrl.description: Root URL of the Dataverse organization; its host is the Dataverse Web API host.

baseLanguage.description: LCID from the location's environmentLanguages list.

securityGroupId.description: Entra group restricting who may use the Dataverse organization. The service returns an empty string for 'unrestricted'; on `provisionInstance` an empty string is rejected with `InvalidSecurityGroupId` and the all-zeros GUID must be sent instead.

friendlyName.description: The organization's own display name, which tracks the environment's `displayName` but is stored separately.

crmGeo.description: Dataverse's own three-letter geo code, which does not match the BAP location name (`OCE` for `unitedstates`).

instanceApiUrl.description: Base URL of the organization's Web API.

instanceState.description: Dataverse-side state of the organization, which lags the environment's own `states.management`.

isDormant.description: True once Dataverse has hibernated an unused organization; the next request wakes it, at the cost of a slow first call.

platformSku.description: Dataverse platform tier serving the organization.

scaleGroup.description: Dataverse scale group hosting the organization.

type.description: Dataverse-side classification of the organization; tracks the environment's `environmentSku` but is a separate, Dataverse-owned value.

hostNameSuffix.description: The Dataverse host suffix `domainName` is prefixed onto to form `instanceUrl`. Varies by crmGeo and by the scale group serving the organization, so it must be read rather than assumed.

webApiVersion.description: Dataverse Web API version this organization serves at `instanceApiUrl/api/data/{webApiVersion}`.

bapSolutionId.description: Id of the platform solution BAPI installed into the organization to wire it to Power Platform. Internal; not a customer solution.

creationTemplates.description: The templates actually installed when the organization was provisioned — the historical record of the create request's `templates`, which is why an environment created with no templates still reports `D365_CDS` here.

modifiedTime.description: When the Dataverse organization itself last changed, which moves independently of the environment's `lastModifiedTime`.

LinkedEnvironmentMetadata.description: The Dataverse organization linked to the environment. Absent entirely when there is none, and absent for several minutes after a create that requested Dataverse — the environment lifecycle operation reports success before this block is readable.

name.description: The value to send as `location` when creating an environment.

Location.description: One BAP location: a named geography, not an Azure region.

LocationList.description: Every location the tenant can see, enabled or not.

code.description: Short internal code for the location.

isDefault.description: True for the one location new environments land in when none is given. Exactly one location is the default, and it follows the tenant's own geography.

isDisabled.description: True where the tenant may not provision at all — sovereign or capacity-restricted geographies show up in the list but cannot be used.

canProvisionDatabase.description: Whether environments here may include Dataverse.

canProvisionCustomerEngagementDatabase.description: Whether Dynamics 365 customer-engagement applications can be installed here, which is narrower than `canProvisionDatabase`.

azureRegions.description: Azure regions selectable via `properties.azureRegion` when creating environments in this location.

enableModelDataSharing.description: Opts the tenant into sharing data for model improvement.

disableDataLogging.description: Stops prompts and responses being logged at all.

ModelExperimentationSettings.description: Whether tenant data may feed model experimentation.

environmentSku.description: The SKU to convert to. `Sandbox` ↔ `Production` is the pair the admin center offers; conversions into `Default` or `Developer` are not supported.

ParentEnvironmentGroup.description: The environment group this environment belongs to. Absent when it belongs to none; the client convention is to read that as the all-zeros GUID.

enableDesktopFlowDataPolicyManagement.description: Allows separate DLP policies covering desktop-flow modules.

PolicySettings.description: Which policy surfaces environment admins may manage.

disableShareWithEveryone.description: Stops makers sharing an app with the whole tenant in one action.

enableGuestsToMake.description: Lets Entra B2B guests author apps, not just run them.

disableMakerMatch.description: Turns off the feature suggesting makers to collaborate with.

disableUnusedLicenseAssignment.description: Stops the platform reassigning premium licences it judges unused.

disableCreateFromImage.description: Blocks generating an app from a screenshot.

disableCreateFromFigma.description: Blocks generating an app from a Figma file.

disableConnectionSharingWithEveryone.description: Stops makers sharing a connection tenant-wide.

disableCopilot.description: Turns off Copilot in the Power Apps studio.

enableCanvasAppInsights.description: Lets makers see Application Insights telemetry for their canvas apps.

enablePlanDesignerCopresence.description: Shows co-editing presence in the plan designer.

enableManagedAppsCliPreview.description: Preview opt-in flag; a tri-state string, not a boolean. `DefaultOn` and `DefaultOff` give the platform default for tenants that have not chosen. Not returned on every tenant.

enableManagedAppsMcsPreview.description: Preview opt-in flag; a tri-state string, not a boolean. `DefaultOn` and `DefaultOff` give the platform default for tenants that have not chosen. Not returned on every tenant.

disableCopilot.description: Turns off Copilot in the flow designer.

disableCopilotWithBing.description: Stops the flow Copilot grounding answers on Bing.

disableFlowRunResubmission.description: Blocks resubmitting a completed flow run, which would repeat its side effects.

enableComputerUseSharedMachines.description: Allows desktop-flow computer use on shared machines.

enableExternalAuthenticationProvidersInP.description: Whether sites may use non-Microsoft identity providers. A string, not a boolean.

enableGenerativeAIFeaturesForSiteUsers.description: Whether generative AI features are offered to site visitors, not only to makers. A string, not a boolean.

securitySettings.description: Tenant security settings. Its members are not described here, and it comes back empty on a tenant that has configured none.

gccCommercialSettings.description: Settings governing GCC tenants reaching commercial cloud services. Returned empty on a commercial tenant.

businessResearchAgent.description: Settings for the business research agent. Comes back empty on a tenant that has configured none.

PowerPlatformSettings.description: The settings tree proper; the flat members alongside it on `TenantSettings` are the older, ungrouped ones.

id.description: The directory object id, except for `type: Service`, where it is the literal string `SYSTEM`.

type.description: `Service` is the platform acting on its own behalf — its `id` and `displayName` are both the literal string `SYSTEM`, not a GUID, so callers must not parse `Principal.id` as a UUID unconditionally. `NotSpecified` is returned for principals the service could not resolve, typically deleted directory objects.

Principal.description: A user, group or service principal. Which members are populated varies by endpoint: `email` and `userPrincipalName` appear on role assignments and on the `provisionInstance` projection, but not on environment reads.

scope.description: The environment the role is granted over.

Properties.description: The assignment: who, what role, and over which scope.

isDisabled.description: True when the tenant cannot install this template; `disabledReason` says why.

isCustomerEngagement.description: True for Dynamics 365 customer-engagement applications, which need a location whose `canProvisionCustomerEngagementDatabase` is true.

isSupportedForResetOperation.description: Whether an environment built from this template can be reset back to empty.

PropertiesItem.description: What the template is and whether it can be used.

RoleAssignment.description: One principal's role in an environment.

RoleDefinition.description: The role being granted. BAPI's environment scope has exactly two: `EnvironmentAdmin` and `EnvironmentMaker`. Dataverse security roles are separate and live in the Dataverse API.

RuntimeEndpoints.description: Per-service regional base URLs for this environment. Clients should read the endpoint for a service from here rather than deriving it from the location, because the Power Virtual Agents endpoint is cluster-specific and differs between two environments in the same geo.

id.description: `Enabled` for a live environment; `Disabled` for one an admin has administratively stopped. `Warning` is a degraded-but-running state — apps and flows still execute, and `runtimeReasonCode` says why the environment is flagged.

runtimeReasonCode.description: Why the runtime was disabled; `NotSpecified` while enabled.

RuntimeEnvironment.description: Runtime state: whether apps and flows in the environment execute.

disableDocsSearch.description: Removes Microsoft Learn results from in-product search.

disableCommunitySearch.description: Removes Power Platform community forum results.

SearchSettings.description: Which sources in-product search may draw on.

Settings.description: Container for the Managed Environments settings; the service nests everything one level deeper under `extendedSettings`.

StatesEnvironment.description: The environment's three independent state machines: administrative, runtime and disaster recovery.

StatesManagementEnvironment.description: Administrative state. `Ready` means no lifecycle operation is running; `Running` means one is, and every mutation will be rejected until it finishes.

shareWithColleaguesUserLimit.description: Cap on how many colleagues an app may be shared with from inside Teams.

TeamsIntegrationSettings.description: How Power Platform behaves inside Teams.

aadCountryGeo.description: Geography derived from the Entra tenant's country. Can differ from `dataStorageGeo` when the tenant was migrated.

dataStorageGeo.description: Where Power Platform stores this tenant's data.

defaultEnvironmentGeo.description: Geography the tenant's default environment lives in.

aadDataBoundary.description: The Entra data boundary the tenant is pinned to (for example `eu` for the EU Data Boundary); `none` when unconstrained.

fedRAMPHighCertificationRequired.description: Whether the tenant demands FedRAMP-High-certified service placement.

Tenant.description: Metadata for the tenant behind the bearer token.

TenantIsolationPolicy.description: The tenant isolation policy governing cross-tenant Power Platform connections.

isDisabled.description: The policy object can exist while disabled; false means isolation is enforced.

allowedTenants.description: Tenants exempted from isolation. An empty list with `isDisabled: false` blocks every cross-tenant connection.

TenantIsolationPolicyProperties.description: Whether isolation is enforced, and which tenants are exempt.

walkMeOptOut.description: Turns off the in-product WalkMe guided tours.

disableCapacityAllocationByEnvironmentAd.description: Reserves capacity allocation to tenant admins; environment admins can no longer draw from the tenant pool.

disableSupportTicketsVisibleByAllUsers.description: Restricts support tickets to the user who raised them.

disableM365Consent.description: Blocks users consenting to Microsoft 365 data access from Power Platform apps.

disableTeamsConsent.description: Blocks the equivalent consent prompt inside Teams.

disableTeamsEnvironmentCreationByNonAdmi.description: Stops non-admins creating the environments Teams provisions on demand.

disableSurveyScreenshots.description: Stops feedback surveys attaching screenshots, which can include business data.

TenantSettings.description: Tenant-wide Power Platform settings. Reads return the complete tree; writes are a merge, so a client managing a subset must send only that subset.

UnblockableConnector.description: A connector DLP policies are not permitted to block.

unblockable.description: Always `true` in this collection: the endpoint lists only unblockable connectors rather than flagging them.

UnblockableConnectorMetadata.description: Why the connector appears in this list.

id.description: `Frequent` puts the environment on the early-release ring; `Moderate` on the standard one.

UpdateCadence.description: How early the environment receives Power Platform service updates.

UsedBy.description: The single user a Developer-SKU environment is provisioned for.

enableDeleteDisabledUserinAllEnvironment.description: Removes a disabled Entra user from every environment at once rather than leaving orphaned records behind.

ValidateCreateEnvironmentDetails.description: Pre-flight check for a create: is this domain name well-formed, free, and is this location real? Both members are required — omitting `environmentLocation` fails the same way as sending a bogus one.

environmentName.description: The environment id. Validated: an unknown id fails with `EnvironmentNotFound`.

ValidateUpdateEnvironmentDetails.description: Pre-flight check for renaming an existing environment's Dataverse domain. Selected over the create variant by sending `environmentName` instead of `environmentLocation`.

id.description: A bare capability name rather than the `/providers/...` resource id real connectors use.

VirtualConnector.description: A platform capability modelled as a connector so DLP can classify it, with no runtime connector behind it — HTTP actions and the like.

iconUri.description: The icon, inline as a `data:` URI rather than a link.

VirtualConnectorMetadata.description: Presentation metadata for the virtual connector.

Error.description: The uniform error envelope. Every 4xx and 5xx uses exactly this shape, on both the `Microsoft.BusinessAppPlatform` and `PowerPlatform.Governance` providers, including the bodies BAPI returns for 500.

ErrorDetail.description: The single error the request failed on; BAPI never returns a list of them.

code.description: Stable machine-readable symbol; the only part of the envelope safe to branch on. Known values include `EnvironmentNotFound`, `EnvironmentGroupNotFound`, `DLPPolicyNotFound`, `OperationNotFound`, `OperationNotStartable`, `DomainNameAlreadyInUse`, `InvalidDomainName`, `EnvironmentLocationUnsupported`, `EnvironmentDisplayNameNotFound`, `InvalidEnvironmentSku`, `InvalidOrMissingDeleteCode`, `InvalidSecurityGroupId`, `InvalidApplicationId`, `InvalidApiVersion`, `InvalidRequestContent`, `InvalidLifecycleOperationRequest`, `ApiPolicyInvalid`, `UrlPatternsNull`, `LinkedEnvironmentForbiddenOperation` and `InternalServerError`.

message.description: Human-readable, and frequently the only place the service enumerates a closed value set: rejections of `location`, `environmentSku` and the delete reason code all list every accepted value in prose. Worth surfacing verbatim rather than replacing with a generic message.

detailUrlType.description: Selects the help article the admin center links from the error. `NotSpecified` in practice.

EnvironmentCapacity.description: Consumption of one capacity type by this environment, as of `updatedOn`.

capacityType.description: The metered resource, for example `Database`, `File` or `Log`.

ratedConsumption.description: Usage after licensing multipliers; this is what counts against the tenant's entitlement, and it can differ from `actualConsumption`.

ClientUris.description: Deep links into the first-party web experiences for this environment.

admin.description: The environment's page in the Power Platform admin center.

maker.description: The environment in the maker portal.

LifecycleOperationsEnforcement.description: Which lifecycle operations this environment will currently accept. Reading it before a mutation is cheaper than provoking the rejection: an operation listed under `disallowedOperations` carries the reason it is blocked.

AllowedOperation.description: A lifecycle operation the environment will accept right now.

DisallowedOperation.description: A lifecycle operation the environment will currently reject, with the reason.

DisallowedOperationReason.description: Why an operation is unavailable on this environment.

type.description: `CdsLink` — blocked because a Dataverse organization is linked; `EnvironmentSkuType` — not available for this SKU; `EnvironmentDisabled` — the environment is administratively disabled; `EnvironmentCmkLinked` — blocked by a customer-managed key; `GovernanceConfig` — blocked by the Managed Environments configuration.

LifecycleOperationType.description: Names one kind of lifecycle operation. The same vocabulary appears in `LifecycleOperation.type`, in `ongoingOperation.type`, and in both halves of `lifecycleOperationsEnforcement`.

id.description: `Create` (an environment create), `Edit` (a property PATCH), `Convert` (a SKU change) and `Delete` are the four raised by the operations in this spec; `EnableGovernanceConfiguration` and `UpdateGovernanceConfiguration` come from the Managed Environments POST. The rest cover backup/restore, disaster recovery, tenant-to-tenant migration and the enterprise-policy links, and are seen mainly inside `lifecycleOperationsEnforcement`. `Provision` appears only there — an environment create raises `Create`.

NotificationMetadata.description: Controls the in-product banner shown to users of the environment, used for trial expiry and migration notices.

ProtectionStatus.description: Who holds the encryption key for the environment's data at rest.

keyManagedBy.description: `Microsoft` until a customer-managed key enterprise policy is linked.

RetentionDetails.description: How long a deleted environment stays recoverable, and how far back its backups reach.

OngoingOperation.description: Present on reads only while a lifecycle operation is in flight, and the cheapest way to discover the operation blocking a mutation: its `links.self.path` is the lifecycleOperations URL to poll, and its `type.id` says what is running. It disappears once the operation reaches a terminal state.

BillingInstrument.description: The Azure subscription and resource group the policy bills to.

provisioningStatus.description: State of the Azure-side resource backing the policy; billing only flows once it is `Succeeded`.

PayAsYouGoPolicy.description: Whether one product's consumption in this environment is metered to the billing instrument instead of drawing on licensed capacity.

PowerAutomatePayAsYouGoPolicy.description: Power Automate meters its three run types separately, so each can be billed pay-as-you-go independently.

LifecycleLinks.description: Resource-relative paths (not absolute URLs) for the operation and its subject.

LifecycleState.description: The operation's state. `NotStarted` → `Running` → `Succeeded`/`Failed`; a short-lived operation can be `Succeeded` on the first poll.

AdminManagementApplicationList.description: Every service principal registered as an admin management application in the tenant.

disableHelpSupportCopilot.description: Turns off the Copilot in the help pane.

useSupportBingSearchByAllUsers.description: Lets help search the public web through Bing, not just Microsoft documentation.

EnvironmentTemplateList.description: The flat, ungrouped rendering of the same templates that api-version 2019-10-01 returns.

ScheduledLifecycleOperation.description: A lifecycle operation the platform has already scheduled against the environment, with the date it will run. Trials and inactive Developer environments carry two: a `Disable` and, a fortnight later, a `Delete`.

type.description: Which operation is scheduled. Unlike `LifecycleOperationType` this is a bare string, not an object with an `id`.

scheduledDateTime.description: When the operation runs if nothing intervenes. Whole seconds, unlike the sub-millisecond timestamps elsewhere on the environment.

canExtend.description: Whether an admin may still push the date back — false once the environment has used up its allowed extensions.

EnvironmentPermission.description: One permission the calling user holds in the environment. The map key is the permission name; this object carries only its label.

displayName.description: Human label. Frequently the key verbatim (`CreateBot`), sometimes spaced (`Read Environment`), and occasionally different from it — `CreateCustomApi` renders as `Create Custom Connector` and `SetDLPPolicy` as `Update DLP Policy`. Display only; branch on the key.

LastActivityRecord.description: One activity timestamp pair. The all-zeros date `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z` is the sentinel for "never" — treat it as no activity, not as a date in year 1.

lastActivityTime.description: When a user last did something. `0001-01-01T00:00:00Z` when there has been no activity.

lastUpdatedTime.description: When the platform last refreshed this figure. Moves on its own schedule and is routinely far newer than `lastActivityTime`, so it says nothing about user activity.

EnvironmentPartnerLastActivity.description: Per-service breakdown behind the rolled-up figure. Each first-party service reports its own last activity independently, and a service with nothing to report still appears with the all-zeros sentinel.

eloLastActivity.description: Environment lifecycle operations — admin activity against the environment itself. Usually the newest of the five, because an environment nobody uses is still edited by admins.

EnvironmentLastActivity.description: When the environment was last used, and by which service. This is what the inactivity policies act on: an environment whose `lastActivity.lastActivityTime` falls far enough behind acquires the `scheduledLifecycleOperations` that disable and then delete it.

lastActivity.description: The rolled-up figure across every service — the newest of the per-service entries.

LifecycleOperationList.description: A page of lifecycle operations, newest first. There is no continuation token or `nextLink`; the service returns the whole filtered set in one response.

EnvironmentGroupList.description: A page of environment groups. Paged with `$top`; there is no continuation token.

CountryDefaultOptIn.description: The default answer to the optional-data-collection consent prompt for one country.

defaultOptIn.description: `Yes` opts users in by default, `No` leaves them opted out until they choose, and `DoNotShow` suppresses the prompt entirely for that country. A string, not a boolean.

CountryDefaultOptInList.description: The full per-country table, returned in one response.

FeatureProperties.description: What the flag controls and where its value came from.

featureDescription.description: Free-text engineering description of the flag. Written for Microsoft's own engineers, not for tenants, and not a stable contract.

settingSource.description: Where the flag's value comes from. `FeatureGate` — a service-side rollout gate — in practice.

Feature.description: One feature gate enabled for the principal. Only enabled flags are listed, so presence in the list *is* the value; there is no boolean to read.

name.description: The flag name. Geo-scoped flags carry the BAP location as a dotted suffix, so the same feature appears once per enabled geo.

type.description: Note the `Microsoft.PowerApps` provider: this BAPI path returns PowerApps-provider resource ids.

FeatureList.description: Every feature gate enabled for the principal, in one response — on the order of a thousand entries.
